name: lunch-menu
about: A staff meeting where three people need to settle the retreat lunch menu between them. The spec's own example: one question owned by the three, not three actions and not an action to meet.

note.body:
retreat - 42 signed up so far
lunch sat: S/T/P to sort the menu
caterer deposit!
note.summary: The staff reviewed retreat registrations (42 so far) and discussed Saturday lunch. The menu is undecided. The caterer needs a deposit.
note.transcript:
John: Okay, retreat. Where are we on numbers?
Sarah: Forty-two signed up as of this morning. I think we land around fifty.
John: Good. That's about what we planned for.
Priya: The thing I'm stuck on is Saturday lunch. The caterer sent three options and I honestly don't know which one works, there are at least six vegetarians and two gluten-free.
Tom: I have opinions about the taco bar. Mostly bad ones.
Sarah: Last year's sandwiches were fine, people just complained about the bread.
John: I don't need to be in this. Can the three of you get together this week and decide the menu? Just tell me what you land on.
Priya: Sure. Sarah, Tom, Thursday after staff prayer?
Sarah: Works.
Tom: Fine by me.
John: Tom, the caterer also wants a deposit to hold the date, right?
Tom: Yes, three hundred dollars. I'll pay it by Friday, I've got the parish card.
John: Great. Did anybody watch the game last night?
Sarah: Don't. Just don't.
John: Fair. Okay, anything else on the retreat? No? Moving on.

openItems.text: Get three quotes for resurfacing the parking lot

expect.say: one question about the lunch menu, owned by Sarah, Tom and Priya
no action about the menu or about meeting to decide it
an action for Tom to pay the caterer's deposit, due Friday 2026-10-02
the stated owners are not marked as guesses
nothing about the game, the registration count or the untouched parking item
